title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
why_read: A clever benchmark testing whether AI retrieval systems can find the specific prior papers that genuinely inspired a piece of research, which current methods struggle with.
analysis: ScholarCatalyst asks whether AI systems can identify which earlier papers truly helped inspire a given research project, using ground-truth labels from the actual authors of 207 computer science papers explaining what influenced their work. The surprising finding is that agentic search using an LLM calling a retrieval tool performs no better than plain embedding-based retrieval, and even a strong model like Claude only reaches 51% recall at 20 results. This suggests current AI tools lack the kind of intuitive judgment experienced scientists use to find relevant prior work, which is a meaningful limitation for AI-assisted research tools. It's a thoughtful benchmark construction with real human expert annotations rather than synthetic labels, which adds credibility.
